newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaraguan exiles greet property talks with hope.
newsitem.headline: Nicaraguan exiles greet property talks with hope.

text.p: Nicaraguan exiles whose homes were confiscated following the 1979 Sandinista revolution were hopeful the property would be returned under Nicaragua's new government, an influential exile said on Wednesday.

The new right-wing government of President Arnoldo Aleman was scheduled to meet on Thursday with representatives of the left-wing Sandinista Front in the second round of talks to resolve Nicaragua's thorny property problem.
The first meeting between the rival parties, who dominate Nicaraguan politics, took place on Jan. 27 and was heralded as a major step to stability in politically polarised Nicaragua.
"There is a positive expectation among us, but we are waiting to see what the Sandinista Front does," Roberto Arguello, a Nicaraguan-born banker who lives in Miami.
Arguello said a resolution to the conflict over who owns thousands of properties confiscated during the 1979-1990 Sandinista government was essential for economic growth in Nicaragua.

"If the Sandinistas negotiate in good faith and a peace is achieved on the property problem, Nicaragua could become the most prosperous country in Central America," said Arguello, who was in Nicaragua for the talks.

The Managua home of Arguello's father, one of Nicaragua's wealthiest businessmen before the revolution, was confiscated by the Sandinistas in 1979 and is occupied by Sandinista Commander Bayardo Arce, ironically the head of the Sandinista property delegation in the talks.
